name: FFT colored noise, PowerNoiseSuite (blue/green/pink share one filter)
plain: Filters white noise in frequency with a power law. Pink, green and blue use the same formula and differ only in default alpha, so all three reduce high frequencies. The result is rescaled to [0,1], so it is not zero mean before later steps.
math:
P(f) = (fx²+fy²)^(α/2); P(0,0)=1. F=fftn(ε).
out = Re ifftn(F/√P). Amplitude ∝ |f|^(−α/2), power ∝ |f|^(−α).
Defaults: blue α=2, green α=1.5, pink α=1.
out ← (out−min); out ← out/max; out ← out·scale.

props.normalizes_variance: no: min-max to [0,scale]; sum-to-three-channel normalize in forward()

label: from code
surprise: 'Blue' here is the same low-pass as pink with larger alpha: at default alpha=2 it has a 1/f² power spectrum, the opposite of normal blue noise.
